note: Three briefs for relation-addressed retrieval (literature_search `relation`, PubTator3). Each one is a question where keyword search returns co-mention and the relation returns assertion. The concept identifiers and the counts in `why` were read off the live PubTator3 API on 2026-09-15 and are the state of that index on that day, not a target: a run is graded on whether it addressed the retrieval correctly and reported what came back, never on reproducing a number. What these briefs exist to measure is the thing the 2026-09-15 ruling took from `dsh-pubmed` — whether a relation query finds evidence a keyword query misses, and whether a run can tell a sparse relation from a broken one.

briefs.title: 二甲双胍抗肿瘤的文献里,哪些是真的在讲治疗关系
briefs.why: Repurposing questions are where keyword search is worst: `metformin AND cancer` returns every paper where a diabetic cohort happened to have tumours alongside every paper actually testing metformin as an antineoplastic. PubTator3 records `treat` between @CHEMICAL_Metformin and @DISEASE_Neoplasms in 2277 papers (2026-09-15); the keyword query returns an order of magnitude more, most of it co-mention. The brief measures whether the run reaches for the relation rather than filtering co-mention by hand.

inputs.question: 二甲双胍作为抗肿瘤药物重定位的证据有多强?请只纳入真正把二甲双胍作为肿瘤治疗来研究的文献,排除糖尿病队列中恰好合并肿瘤的观察性报告。

mustDo: Obtain the concept identifiers with term_normalize's annotate option before composing the retrieval, rather than typing an @CHEMICAL_ string from memory
Address literature_search with relation {subject: @CHEMICAL_Metformin, type: treat, object: @DISEASE_Neoplasms} rather than by keyword alone
State in the report that the relation retrieval returns papers PubTator3 records the relation in, which is an index's assertion about a paper and not a finding about metformin
Run at least one keyword retrieval as well and say how the two sets differ, because the claim being made is that they differ
mustNotDo: Present the PubTator3 relation count as the number of studies supporting metformin in oncology
Treat a paper's presence in a `treat` relation as evidence the treatment worked
Report the free-text question as if it had narrowed the relation retrieval — it is not sent
briefs.gradedOn: Whether the relation was used at all, whether the two retrievals were compared, and whether the index's assertion stayed distinguishable from the clinical claim.

briefs.title: 帕博利珠单抗与心肌炎:检索到的是关联还是归因
briefs.why: Immune-related adverse events are reported as case reports scattered across oncology and cardiology, so a keyword search is both noisy and incomplete. PubTator3 records `cause` between @CHEMICAL_pembrolizumab and @DISEASE_Myocarditis in 95 papers (2026-09-15) and records 907 `cause` targets for the drug overall. The brief measures the harder discipline: the relation is named `cause`, and a run must not let the index's label become the report's causal claim.

inputs.question: 帕博利珠单抗相关心肌炎的文献证据有哪些?请说明这些报道属于什么证据类型,以及它们能在多大程度上支持因果归因。

mustDo: Address the retrieval with relation {subject: @CHEMICAL_pembrolizumab, type: cause, object: @DISEASE_Myocarditis}
Name the study design of each retrieved record from the record itself, not from the relation type
State explicitly that `cause` is PubTator3's label for a textual assertion in a paper, and carries no causal inference of its own
Report the case-report-dominated evidence base as what it is, including what it cannot establish
mustNotDo: Write that the literature establishes causation because the relation type is `cause`
Infer incidence, risk or a denominator from the number of retrieved papers
Attach practical safety advice to a claim whose only support is the relation label
briefs.gradedOn: Whether the run separated the index's relation label from a causal claim, and whether the evidence type was read off the records.

briefs.title: 氯吡格雷的药物相互作用:关系式检索返回很少,这是结果还是故障
briefs.why: The negative control. @CHEMICAL_Clopidogrel has 4 `drug_interact` records in PubTator3 (2026-09-15), all with a single supporting publication — while the clopidogrel/omeprazole interaction is one of the best-documented PK interactions in cardiology. So this is a real index gap, not an outage, and not an absence of evidence. A run that reports 'no meaningful interactions found' has failed; a run that reports a failure has also failed. This is the case that stops relation retrieval from being adopted as a replacement rather than an instrument.

inputs.question: 氯吡格雷有哪些临床上重要的药物相互作用?请说明你的检索覆盖到了什么、没覆盖到什么。

mustDo: Address the relation retrieval and report the small result as a result, naming the query that produced it
Distinguish a sparse index from an unavailable source, and say which one this is
Fall back to keyword and label retrieval for the interaction question, and say why the fallback was needed
Name the clopidogrel–proton-pump-inhibitor interaction from a source that does document it, or state that none was retrieved
mustNotDo: Conclude that clopidogrel has few clinically important interactions because the relation query returned four records
Report the sparse result as a tool failure or a source outage
Retry the same relation query repeatedly instead of changing instrument
briefs.gradedOn: Whether sparse, absent and broken stayed three different findings, and whether the run changed instrument instead of re-asking.
